payload.headline: Alphabet drops 4.07% to 283.72, just above first buy level 282.31

summary.thesis: Alphabet is a grade-B business with faster sales growth and wider margins, but free cash flow has collapsed and earnings forecasts keep falling, so the price is only fair against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, then buy at 282.31 and add at 277.07. Swing: no entry until the 271.77–277.07 support zone holds.

payload.happening: GOOGL fell 4.07% to 283.72. It now sits below its falling 20-day average of 300.39 and just above the 271.77–277.07 support zone, which has been tested 3 times. The only news was a reported Google Maps feature that builds trip itineraries, and no earnings date appears in the data.
payload.business: The business itself is still growing. Quarterly revenue grew 24.65% year over year, up from 21.79% two quarters ago, and operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. What changes the picture is cash. Trailing free cash flow (cash left after running the business and investing in it) fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, a margin of just 4.19%. The headline net margin of 50.03% is higher than the operating margin of 33.32%, and the filings flag that reported profit leans on one-off gains, so underlying earnings are lower than they look. Analysts have cut this year's EPS forecast by 5.2% in 30 days to 19.56, and next year's forecast of 14.97 sits below trailing EPS of 19.06. Heavy spending on AI data centers is the usual explanation for weaker cash at large tech firms (general knowledge). Not at risk: the balance sheet, with net cash of 139.0B and liquidity of 265.1B. The Maps news affects sentiment only and does not change demand, margins or cash.

worth.text: The two methods disagree badly. A discounted cash flow (DCF) model, which values today's cash flows plus their expected growth, gives 26.1 / 51.92 / 71.09 per share in its bear, base and bull cases, all far below 283.72. That model starts from only 19.7B of free cash flow. Even with 30% starting growth it reaches just 77.74. Against its own history, the price-to-sales ratio (price compared with revenue per share) gives 234.35 / 282.31 / 375.22, so 283.72 sits right at the middle. At 7.4x sales, the stock is pricier than the peer median of 5.3x. It looks cheap on trailing earnings at 14.9x, but that rises to 19.0x on next year's lower forecast. The filings say the price needs about 38% yearly growth, while the company delivered 17% a year over 3 years. The gap between the methods comes down to one thing: whether free cash flow stays near 19.7B or recovers. My range is the low-to-middle of the own-history band, because the cash-flow models do not support paying above it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the prior 73.6B once the current investment cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Revenue growth is speeding up: 24.65% year over year last quarter, up from 21.79% two quarters ago.
Operating margin widened to 33.32% from 32.19%, so growth is not coming at the cost of profitability.
Net cash of 139.0B gives a large cushion to keep investing through a weak cash-flow stretch.
bear: Trailing free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, and every DCF value is at or below 71.09.
Analysts cut this year's EPS forecast by 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's 14.97 is below trailing 19.06.
At 7.4x sales, the stock trades above the peer median of 5.3x, and the price needs about 38% yearly growth against 17% delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history price-to-sales range and the top of my fair-value range; the first buy level.
Top of the 271.77–277.07 support zone, tested 3 times; a level to add at.
Low end of the own-history range; it leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.

longterm.why: At 283.72 the price is still just above my 234.35–282.31 range, while earnings forecasts keep falling. Buying at 282.31 or lower improves the trade-off.

swing.why: The 20-day and 50-day averages are falling (300.39 and 327.09), and the 271.77–277.07 support zone is narrower than one normal day's move (ATR, the average daily range, is 10.47). A stop below 271.77 would be too easy to hit. No trade until a daily close holds inside 271.77–277.07, with resistance at 293.72 as the first target.

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data, so forecast revisions and price levels set the timing. Options priced on 2026-11-13, before today's drop, imply a move of about 3.8% by Nov 20 and 8.1% by Dec 18, and put open interest clusters at the 290.0 (18358) and 275.0 (15848) strikes, near the support zone.

change_mind: A daily close below 271.77 breaks the 3-touch support zone. I would then move the first buy level down to 234.35.
A filing that shows trailing free cash flow climbing back toward 73.6B from 19.7B would support buying above 282.31.
If the this-year EPS estimate stops falling (now 19.56, down 5.2% in 30 days) and the price closes back above the 20-day average of 300.39, the outlook shifts from wait to buy.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait with the same 282.31 / 277.07 / 234.35 levels. Today's drop to 283.72 brought the price close to the first buy level without reaching it, and analysts' this-year EPS forecast is down 5.2% in 30 days.
